title: Independent Events and Conditional Probability
seo_title: Geometry Independent and Conditional Probability Worksheets (TEKS G.13C)
standard_text: G.13C identify whether two events are independent and compute the probability of the two events occurring together with or without replacement; G.13D apply conditional probability in contextual problems; G.13E apply independence in contextual problems
meta_desc: Free Geometry probability worksheets for Texas TEKS G.13C–G.13E: independent events, conditional probability, two-way tables and drawing with and without replacement. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Independent: P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B).
key_sub: P(B | A) = P(A and B) ÷ P(A).
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Events are independent if one does not change the other: P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B).
  • Conditional probability: P(B | A) = P(A and B) ÷ P(A).
  • Without replacement, the second draw has one fewer item.
  • P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B).

Examples

Example

Draw 2 red from 5 red and 3 blue without replacement

5/8 × 4/7

Answer: 20/56 = 5/14

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Treating dependent events as independentWithout replacement, update the second fraction.
Dividing by the wrong totalGiven A, divide by A's total.
Counting the overlap twiceSubtract P(A and B).

items.q: P(A) = 0.2, P(B) = 0.4 and P(A and B) = 0.1. Find P(A or B).
items.e: Addition Rule: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B) = 0.2 + 0.4 − 0.1 = 0.5. Subtract the overlap so it is not counted twice.

items.q: One card is drawn from a standard 52-card deck. What is the probability it is red or a face card (J, Q, K)?
items.e: 26 red + 12 face cards − 6 red face cards = 32. 32/52 = 813.
